infŏro , āre, v. a. in-forum,
I.to accuse in a court of justice: Curc. Quaeso ne me incomities. Ly. Licetne inforare, si incomitiare haud licet? Curc. Non inforabis me quidem (with double meaning, in mal. part.; cf. “1. inforo),” Plaut. Curc. 3, 30 sq.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
